thread:
Aisha: Quick design sync — running through the regression diff list and the compact vs expanded density for prompt-sets. Need UX + a11y calls on the approval flow microcopy. Thoughts?

Matt: I sketched two variants: compact list (single-line diffs) and stacked cards (more context). Compact saves vertical space but loses diff context when there are inline changes.

Priya: Eng note: compact rows faster to render and allow virtualized list, but inline diffs need expandable detail panel. Also bulk-approve needs server-side pagination support.

Darren: Accessibility: compact rows must preserve focus order and expose a keyboard affordance to expand diffs. Screen-reader label idea: "Show more changes for <prompt name>". Also color contrast for added/removed tokens is low in current mock.

Matt: Proposed microcopy for approval modal:

"Approve selected prompt changes"
"This will apply changes to production prompts. Review diffs carefully."

or shorter:
"Apply changes to active prompt set"

Aisha: I prefer the slightly longer copy for clarity. Can we add a small 'why this matters' link?

Priya: Implementation detail: modal needs an extra confirmation step for destructive changes (remove prompt), and API needs an idempotency token. Backend team suggests: add 'force' flag only for owners.

EvalBot: Automated note — recent eval run #472 failed on regression suite "checkout_flow"; 3/12 tests degraded. See /evals/472

Darren: On the compact diffs, keyboard shortcut proposal:

```
j/k: move selection
Enter: expand
Space: toggle approve
```

Matt: Also UX nit — bulk approve CTA shouldn't be primary unless user selects >1 item. Otherwise it looks like a big destructive action.

Aisha: Decision proposal:
- Default to compact list with expandable diffs
- Add explicit 'Expand all' control and keyboard support
- Approval modal uses long copy + 'why this matters' link
- Bulk approve CTA disabled unless >1 selected and requires confirmation for deletions

Priya: Sounds good. I'll add API contract and a migration plan for pagination. I'll also add metrics event names.

Matt: I'll push updated mock to Figma and tag @Aisha @Priya. Will add contrast tweaks for diffs.

Darren: I'll write a short a11y checklist and run with VoiceOver.

Aisha: Thanks all — aim to ship this in next sprint. :rocket:
